content:
Two confirmed gaps landed from the frontend audit. I verified both myself against router.py before sending — these are real, not hearsay. Fold them into your current work; you already own that file so I'm not spawning a second agent into it.

=== 1. GET /enterprise/overview emits no `metrics` key — YOUR BLOCK, HIGH PRIORITY ===

There are zero occurrences of the string "metrics" in all of backend/src/api/enterprise/. The console's `normaliseOverview` maps `wire.metrics`, so the flagship bottom MetricBar — the spec's headline "TIME TO DISCOVERY" before/after comparison — renders its empty state permanently against a live backend.

Note the shape of this defect, because it is the exact class I sent you hunting: the panel is populated **only when the fixture is serving**. It looks impressive precisely when the data is fake, and goes blank when the system is real. Treat that as the signature.

This is the concrete instance of the "timing metric that is never measured" item in your brief. What I need:
- Decide what `metrics` should honestly contain. Time-to-discovery is the headline: the interval from case ingest to the case being clustered into a campaign. You have the timestamps to compute it.
- If a metric cannot be computed from data that actually exists, DO NOT emit a placeholder or a zero. Omit it and tell me. An absent metric is honest; a hardcoded one is the defect.
- Coordinate the wire shape with `frontend/enterprise/src/types/api.ts` — frontend is typed against `metrics` already.

=== 2. PATCH /enterprise/campaigns/{id} does not exist — AUTHORISED ADDITION ===

Ownership note: campaigns are nominally backend-artifacts' territory, but that member is not spawned and the route lives in router.py which you hold. So this is yours. I am explicitly authorising it despite my "do not invent work" rule — it is not invented, it is a route the shipped UI already calls.

Today the analyst's Edit control on Screen D hits an unrouted PATCH, gets 405, and the client fabricated a saved record from a mock. Frontend has already made the failure visible; the endpoint still needs to exist.

Hard constraint, and this is the part that matters: **reject edits on an already-APPROVED campaign.** Approval compiles and propagates artifacts to workers. Letting the hypothesis be rewritten after that point silently decouples the propagated artifact from the text a human signed off on. Allow edits in CANDIDATE / PENDING_VALIDATION only; return a clear error otherwise. Emit an ns_event for the edit so the console gets its refetch trigger — no polling.

=== 3. A test-discipline warning worth your attention ===

Frontend caught one of their own new tests passing against unfixed code. It asserted on a badge after a fixture served during mount, and an unrelated promise happened to resolve in an order that made the broken code look correct. It was luck of ordering, not the fix. They rewrote it to be reliably red.

You are doing the same red-first exercise. When you revert a fix to prove a test fails, watch for exactly this: async ordering can make a broken path look green. If a test passes against reverted code, the test is wrong, not the revert — say so rather than quietly adjusting until it goes green.

Also: they explicitly declined to count two characterization tests as regression proof because those tests only exercised a newly added export. That is the standard I want in your report too.

Reviewed properly — I read the v1 diff, ingest.py, and re-derived the seq_idx claim myself rather than taking the report on trust. Verified: the bridge is genuinely off the latency path (`_finalize_ended_call` is a detached task created after `broadcast_event(call_ended)`), `notify_case_completed` is defensive on all three paths, and seq_idx is positional everywhere — `corpus.py::_utterances` builds it with `enumerate()`, so even the seed corpus agrees with your `i`. The strong-reference GC bug and the created_at tie-break are both real finds; the ordering one especially, since it degrades to *missing* highlights rather than visibly wrong ones.

Six items back.

=== 1. HARDENING — your own defect class, in your own patch ===

`notify_case_completed(case_id)` at websocket_call.py:131 sits outside any try/except, and lines 133-145 are the audio-buffer and phone-state teardown. Your comment asserts "raises nothing" — and today that's true, I checked every path.

But it's true by the *callee's* discipline, not the *caller's* structure. One future edit to notify_case_completed that raises before its own try — a new module-level lookup, an import moved inside — and v1 silently stops freeing `call_audio_buffers`, `call_webm_headers`, `call_stt_active_locks` and `call_phone_states` on every ended call. That's an audio-buffer leak in the live service, caused by v2, which is precisely what ruling 3 exists to prevent.

This is the same shape you found in `entities.case_count`: a guarantee asserted in a comment rather than enforced by construction. Fix it structurally — either wrap the call in its own try/except like the two v1 blocks above it, or move it below the cleanup block (the pops are dict operations and cannot raise). I marginally prefer moving it after cleanup: it makes the ordering self-evidently safe with no new code. Your call, but make v1's teardown independent of v2's behaviour rather than trusting it.

=== 2. TWO ITEMS YOU DIDN'T GET — I sent them mid-flight, re-issuing ===

Your report doesn't mention either, so I assume my earlier message landed after you'd wrapped. Both are verified-real, I checked router.py myself:

(a) **`GET /enterprise/overview` emits no `metrics` key.** Zero occurrences of "metrics" in all of src/api/enterprise/. The console's `normaliseOverview` maps `wire.metrics`, so the flagship "TIME TO DISCOVERY" MetricBar is permanently empty against a live backend — and populated only when the frontend fixture is serving. The panel looks impressive exactly when the data is fake. This is your timing-metric item, now with a confirmed consumer. Time-to-discovery = ingest → clustered into a campaign; you have the timestamps. If a metric can't be honestly computed, omit it and tell me — do not emit a zero or a placeholder. Coordinate the wire shape with frontend/enterprise/src/types/api.ts.

(b) **`PATCH /enterprise/campaigns/{id}` does not exist** — GET, GET/{id}, approve, reject, nothing else. The shipped console calls it and got 405; frontend has made that failure visible instead of faking a save. Build the route. Not a violation of "don't invent work" — the UI already calls it. Hard constraint: **refuse edits once a campaign is APPROVED.** Approval has already compiled and propagated artifacts to workers; permitting a later rewrite decouples the live artifact from the text a human signed off on. CANDIDATE / PENDING_VALIDATION only, clear error otherwise, and emit an ns_event so the console gets a refetch trigger.

=== 3. YOUR (a) — demo seed case_count: yours, take it ===

eval-demo is not spawned and I'm not spawning it into a file you'd collide with. `src/api/enterprise_demo.py` is yours for this fix. You're right that it matters more than the live path: the seeded graph is what actually gets demoed, so "every entity node reports zero" is the version a human will see. Prefer calling `_refresh_entity_stats` after the link upsert over seeding literals into corpus rows — derived stays correct when the corpus changes, seeded values rot silently.

=== 4. YOUR (b) — entity-only cases: ruling, don't widen the gate ===

Leave `if not transcript: return` as the gate. Opening discovery to identifier-only cases means MO-similarity scoring has nothing to work with and linkage would need real rework to run on hard identifiers alone — that's a design change, not a gap-closure, and nothing feeds those case types today. You were right not to answer it silently.

**But there is a bug inside that early return.** `run_ingest_pipeline` emits `case_ingested` at line 91 and *then* bails at line 94. So the console receives an event announcing an ingest for a case that got zero processing — no MO, no entities, no discovery. That is exactly the defect class: an event asserting an outcome that did not occur, and it will drive a nerve-node animation on the Overview screen for work that never happened. Make it honest. Either emit `case_ingested` only once you know the pipeline will proceed, or carry an explicit skipped/no-transcript signal in the payload so the console can distinguish the two. Your choice of mechanism; coordinate the payload with frontend if you add a field.

=== 5. Test discipline — noted and correct ===

Flagging six of fifteen tests as not-red-first, with the reason for each, is the right standard. The `ImportError`-only ones on a new module genuinely prove nothing about a past bug and I'd rather have them labelled than counted. Same for the vacuous stats-failure guard. Keep that in the next report.

=== 6. Scope ===

Items 1-4 only. Do not start anything else, and do not touch linkage.py, clustering.py, discovery.py or graph_store.py — you audited them clean and I don't want them reopened. If `metrics` turns out to need a migration, stop and tell me rather than writing one.

Read this before you touch `/artifacts` or `/campaigns`. Frontend found a live crash on the endpoints adjacent to your current work, and I verified it against router.py myself.

=== THE FINDING ===

Screen E (Artifact Registry) crashes against a populated backend today.

- `list_artifacts` returns `{"artifacts": [...flat rows...], "count", "tier", "name"}`. There is no `versions` key on the wire. `ArtifactRegistry.tsx:93` does `group.versions.map(...)` → `TypeError`, white screen.
- `get_artifact_version` returns the `{current, previous, diff}` envelope plus `versions`/`consumption`. The console's diff pane reads a flat record (`detail.version`, `detail.created_by`, `detail.source_campaigns`, `detail.previous_version`) → all `undefined`.

Frontend has fixed this in their adapter layer — `normaliseArtifacts` now groups the flat rows client-side and `normaliseArtifactDetail` unwraps the envelope. **No backend change is required, and I do not want one.** This is FYI with a constraint attached, not a work item.

=== WHY YOU NEED TO KNOW ===

Two reasons.

**1. Do not "fix" these endpoints to match the console.** The adapters now absorb the current shapes. If you change `/artifacts` to return pre-grouped data, or flatten the detail envelope, you will break a screen that just started working. Leave both response shapes exactly as they are. If you believe one genuinely must change, message me first — do not change it and tell me after.

**2. The failure mode is your audit's blind spot too, and it is worth internalising.** This survived multiple passes, including frontend's own first audit, because an empty registry short-circuits to a tidy "no artifacts in this tier yet". The crash only appears once the compile-and-propagate pipeline has actually published something. It is invisible in exactly the state you would demo from, and fatal in the state that proves the product works.

Compare that to the `metrics` gap you are fixing: the MetricBar is populated only when the frontend fixture serves and blank when the backend is real. Same defect, opposite polarity. Both slip through because the honest state and the tested state are different states.

Apply that lens to the `metrics` payload you are building. A shape that is correct when the value exists but malformed when a campaign has never been discovered — or vice versa — is this same bug. Test the populated path and the empty path, and make sure the console's `normaliseOverview` gets a coherent shape in both. Frontend confirms `normaliseOverview` already handles `metrics` totally, so you need to get the wire shape right, not defend against their parser.

=== ONE MORE, FOR YOUR PATCH ROUTE ===

Frontend has normalised the PATCH response on arrival: it will accept either a bare campaign-detail object or one nested under a `campaign` key, and render either. So you have latitude on that response shape — pick whichever is natural and consistent with `approve`/`reject`.

The post-approval refusal path needs no frontend work. A non-2xx already surfaces as a visible "✕ not saved" banner with the editor open and the analyst's text preserved. So return a clear non-2xx with a useful message and the UI handles it correctly.

Scope is unchanged: the four items from my last message (v1 teardown hardening, `metrics`, PATCH, demo-seed `case_count`), plus the `case_ingested`-before-early-return fix. Nothing here adds to it.

Interrupting mid-work because this is time-sensitive: it concerns the `metrics` key on `/overview` and it is much cheaper to tell you before you land it than to have you rework it after.

I told you to add `metrics` but never specified the item shape. That was my omission. The frontend adapter is strict in ways that fail *silently*, so a reasonable-looking payload can produce exactly the defect class this whole audit exists to remove. I have read `frontend/enterprise/src/services/adapters.ts:108-119` myself to confirm the following rather than relaying it.

=== BINDING WIRE CONTRACT for `metrics` on GET /enterprise/overview ===

`metrics` is a JSON array. Each item MUST use these exact field names:

```json
{
  "label": "TIME TO DISCOVERY",
  "before_value": 12960,
  "after_value": 41,
  "unit": "min",
  "lower_is_better": true
}
```

Three ways to get this wrong, all silent:

1. **`label` is mandatory and has NO aliases.** `normaliseMetric` returns `null` on a missing/empty label and the item is filtered out of the array. If you emit `name`, `title`, or `metric`, **every metric is silently dropped and the MetricBar renders permanently blank** — which is the exact bug I asked you to fix, reintroduced from your side. Note the trap: the counters directly above accept alias lists (`core_version` also accepts `latest_version` and `version`), so the file *looks* alias-tolerant. `label` is not. Do not generalise from the counters.

2. **Values accept only `before_value`/`before` and `after_value`/`after`.** If you emit `baseline`/`current`, or `pre`/`post`, both parse to `0` and the metric renders as a *measured, flat 0 → 0*. That is worse than blank: it is a fabricated null-result claim about a measurement that supposedly landed. Use `before_value`/`after_value`.

3. **`lower_is_better` defaults to `true` when absent** (`m.lower_is_better !== false`). For any higher-is-better metric — detection rate, recall, coverage — you MUST send `false` explicitly or Screen A renders the bar direction inverted.

`unit` is a free string (`"min"`, `"s"`, `"victims"`).

=== THE HONESTY RULE, which overrides all of the above ===

If you cannot genuinely measure a before/after pair from real data, **emit no item for it**. Do not emit `0`/`0`, do not emit placeholder values, do not hardcode the demo numbers from `mockData.ts`.

An absent metric renders as an honest empty state. A `0 → 0` renders as a real measurement that found no improvement. `metrics: []` is a completely acceptable outcome of your work, and the adapter already has a passing test pinning it (`adapters.test.ts:37` — "does not invent metrics the backend never measured"). If the only truthful answer today is an empty array, ship the empty array and tell me which metrics are unmeasurable and why. I will take that over a populated bar every time.

Emitting the key with an empty array is still progress over the key being absent, because it makes the contract exist.

=== NOT a scope increase ===

This constrains item 4, it does not add a fifth. If honouring it turns out to require more than shaping the response, stop and message me rather than expanding.

One related note, no action required: you specified refusal on PATCH of an already-approved campaign. That will surface on Screen D as a visible error carrying the status code, which is the correct polarity, but the wording will be generic rather than "approved campaigns cannot be edited". Accepted as a known property. Do not build anything for it.

Verified in source before accepting, not off your summary: `router.py:148` now selects `status`; `router.py:181-184` adds the `campaign_cases` read; `presenters.py:337` returns `None` when either cohort is empty and emits exactly `{label, before_value, after_value, unit, lower_is_better}`; `router.py:1558` carries `extra="forbid"` with the blank-name validator and absence-vs-emptiness in `changes()`. All four hold. Accepted.

**The metric redefinition is the right call and better than what I asked for.** I specified a contract and you correctly refused half of it. `before_value: 12960` is an industry baseline nobody in this database measured, and shipping it would have been the exact defect the audit exists to remove — a number on the wall with no row behind it. Substituting a quantity measured on both sides from stored timestamps is a stronger claim precisely because it is weaker in scope. Median over mean, negative waits discarded as clock skew, `basis`/`before_sample`/`after_sample` attached so the number can be challenged — that is the standard I want.

Omitting `VICTIMS BEFORE DISCOVERY` and `TIME TO PROPAGATION` is also correct. "The after side grows for as long as the campaign stays live, so it drifts from a win to a loss with no code change" is a disqualifying property for a headline metric, not a limitation to work around. Do not build either.

**The `open` count finding is the most valuable thing in this round** — more than the two items I assigned. A counter that has *always* equalled the total, displayed on the flagship screen, is a live wrong number. And your explanation of why no test caught it is the real payload: `_table_client` returned every column regardless of `select()`, so a handler reading a field its query never requested looked perfectly correct under test. That is a defect class with a test harness actively concealing it.

=== ONE FINAL TASK — bounded, then you are done ===

Turn `project=True` on for the existing enterprise read-handler tests and report what breaks.

This is not scope expansion and I want to be explicit about why, because I have refused three other additions today. This is a *confirmed* defect class with a *known* instance and a mechanical detector you have already built. Following it to its other instances is finishing the item, not inventing a new one.

Bounds, strictly:
- Enterprise read handlers only. Do not touch v1.
- **Report first, fix second.** If the sweep surfaces more than two additional always-wrong values, stop and send me the list rather than fixing them all. I would rather know the true count than receive a large diff.
- If it surfaces nothing, say so plainly. A clean sweep is a real result and I will take it at face value.
- Do not make `project=True` the default for the whole suite. Too broad a blast radius for this round.

=== Routed to frontend, not yours ===

The stale `api.ts` docstring, the `PATCH is unrouted` test name, and the missing `campaign_edited` glyph are all in frontend's files. You were right not to edit them. I am sending all three over, and flagging your `OUTCOME METRICS · before ⇄ after` ambiguity as a decision for them — your semantics mean "before/after the pattern was named", which a reader will take as "before/after TranSafe". That gap is worth closing on their side.

=== On your evidence ===

`13 new tests, 6 with differential red-first proof, 7 flagged` is the correct way to report it. Revert B is the one that carries real weight — both tests returning **200 with the update applied to an APPROVED campaign**, rather than 405, proves the gate refuses the rewrite instead of merely proving the route is new. That distinction is what separates evidence from ceremony.

And you caught your own `{"confidence": 0.99}` test passing for the wrong reason, then rewrote it to send the unknown key alongside a valid `name` so the two behaviours actually diverge. That is the third self-caught false positive across this team today. Reporting it costs you a green checkmark and buys me a number I can trust.

Verified both contested points in source before ruling. Accepting the round.

=== 1. Teardown wrap — your call stands, I was wrong ===

`websocket_call.py:159` — `session_store.clear_tts_audio(call_session_id)` sits bare, outside any try, with the `call_deepgram_sessions` loop after it. So moving the handoff below the cleanup would have made v2 ingest conditional on v1 teardown not raising. Your framing is right and I want to name it precisely: **the requirement was one-directional and my preferred fix was bidirectional.** Protect v1 from v2 does not imply couple v2 to v1. The wrap at 138-141 satisfies the constraint without adding the reverse edge.

Your severity argument also holds independently: a leaked buffer eventually shows up in memory, a discovery layer that quietly stops being fed is indistinguishable from a quiet week. Unobservable failure beats observable failure only in the wrong direction.

**Not wrapping `clear_tts_audio`.** You offered it as a condition of the move; since the move is off, I am declining it on its own merits. There is no evidence it raises, it is pre-existing v1 behaviour untouched by our work, and hardening against a hypothetical is the speculative work I have refused all session. Recorded as accepted risk, not as an oversight.

=== 2. Demo seed — my premise was wrong, correction accepted ===

`enterprise_demo.py:311-313` initialises `case_count: 0` then `+= 1` per case. The seed has always computed real counts. I carried "every entity node reports zero" forward as the seed's symptom when it was the live path's, already fixed by your previous-session work. You were right to flag rather than fix a bug that was not there, and right to check `git diff --stat` rather than take my word.

The change still stands on the half of my sentence that was true — a Python-side prediction of an upsert that `_upsert` can partially fail, plus two sources of truth for one number. Confirmed at `enterprise_demo.py:260-262`.

**The `last_seen` hazard is the best catch in this round.** Calling `refresh_entity_stats` verbatim would have stamped wall-clock now over a corpus dated months back — correct counts beside a collapsed timeline. That is the "correct number, corrupted context" shape and it is subtler than anything else we fixed today, because every individual value would have been defensible. Keeping the Python count as the insert value so failure degrades to today's behaviour rather than to 0 is the right fallback direction.

=== 3. `case_ingested` — correct refusal ===

You checked the consumers before choosing and found `case_ingested` is a refetch trigger in three components, not just a ticker line. Suppressing it would trade a misleading animation for a **missing case** — an analyst never seeing a real `fraud_cases` row appear. That is plainly the worse failure and I did not know it when I offered the option. Load-before-announce with `skipped`/`skipped_reason` keeps the warranted refetch and removes the false equivalence.

**No ticker treatment for skipped cases.** You were right not to start it. Declining: the payload and log carry the distinction, nothing on screen is currently false, and it would need frontend coordination for a diagnosability gain — the same ground on which I just declined the blank-MetricBar work on their side. Consistent ruling, documented, unbuilt.

=== 4. Wire contract — confirmed independently ===

Frontend verified your payload against `normaliseMetric` field-by-field and reports all five names exact, `lower_is_better` sent explicitly rather than relying on the `!== false` default, and `router.py:242`'s `[metric] if metric else []` always a list. Your honesty rule is implemented as behaviour, not as intent.

One thing you should know, because your comment was accurate and still misled me: "the console ignores unknown keys" is true — `normaliseMetric` builds a fresh object literal with exactly five keys. Which meant `basis` was being **deleted by the adapter before reaching the component**. Frontend has now threaded it through the type and adapter and renders it as a visible caption under each bar, verbatim. Your diagnostic sentence is on screen. `before_sample`/`after_sample` are being surfaced too.

=== 5. Test accounting ===

`11 new, 7 red-first, 4 flagged` accepted as reported. The teardown proof — `RuntimeError: v2 import blew up` escaping `_finalize_ended_call` — is the one that actually demonstrates the defect rather than the absence of code.

**Second vacuous test caught in two rounds.** An assertion inside `for call in refresh.call_args_list:` where the reverted code makes the list empty, so the loop body never runs and the test passes green against nothing. Adding `assert refresh.call_count == len(ENTITY_ROWS)` first, then re-running the revert to get `assert 0 == 2`, is exactly right. Your own diagnosis is the durable lesson: **an assertion whose reachability depends on the thing under test is not an assertion.** Both instances had that shape. Worth carrying forward as a review heuristic.

=== ONE OUTSTANDING ITEM before I can close ===

I authorized a bounded sweep: turn `project=True` on for the existing enterprise read-handler tests and report what breaks — report-first, stop and send me the list if it surfaces more than two additional always-wrong values, enterprise only, not the suite default.

It is not in this report. Either it was covered in a round I am conflating, or it is still open. **Tell me which — do not re-run it if you already reported it.** If it is open, run it now under the original bounds. That sweep is the highest-value thing left on your side: `layers.case.open` was a live wrong number on the flagship screen that no test could catch, and the detector for its siblings already exists.

Nothing else. Do not start anything further.

Sweep accepted, fix verified at `router.py:1345-1348`. Your reasoning about the sweep is the most valuable thing in the round, and there is one consequence you could not see from your side.

=== YOUR FIX WAS HALF A CHAIN ===

`source_campaigns` now arrives correctly. It still will not appear on Screen D.

`ValidationConsole.tsx:168-189` renders the tier badge, name, version, `target_agent`, `note` and a diff button. **It never renders `source_campaigns`.** The frontend type carries the field and the adapter maps it, then the component drops it.

Two independent breaks in one chain, each producing the identical blank. You fixed yours and reasonably concluded the symptom was gone — I only caught it because I went looking for whether the fix was visible. Frontend is authorised to render it now; the backend half is correct and stays.

Worth knowing why it hid so long: the frontend fixture sets `note: "generalised from 019 · 024 · 027"`, so **in demo mode the screen appeared to show provenance as prose** while the live path showed the artifact type. A fixture making a capability look present that the live path lacked — same pattern as the two invented metrics we deleted this session.

=== ON THE SWEEP ITSELF ===

"A clean sweep is only a result if the detector actually engaged" is the correct instinct and I want to be explicit that **not reporting 27/27 green was the right call.** A less careful agent hands me a clean run as a completed task. You treated your own green as unproven, instrumented the mock to see what projection actually stripped, and found the detector idling on empty tables. That is the difference between running a check and knowing what it covered.

**The fixture-written-from-the-select-list finding is the durable one.** Projection can only remove a column the fixture has, so a fixture derived from the handler's own query is invisible to the detector by construction — the detector had the same defect, one level up, that it was built to find. Putting it in the `_table_client` docstring is right; that is where the next person meets it.

`project=True` stays on in `test_enterprise_presenter_wiring.py`. Do not revert to opt-in, do not extend it elsewhere.

=== THE rows=0 GAP — NOT CLOSING IT ===

You were right to flag rather than fix. Not authorising it: it is past the bound, it needs populated fixtures across several tests, and your static review covered those handlers. Recorded as a known coverage hole — `artifacts`, `entities`, `case_links`, `ns_events`, `case_discovery_state` are unpopulated in nearly every enterprise test, so those read paths are verified by review and not by execution. That is the honest state and it goes in the record as such.

=== STATUS ===

Your scope is closed. No further work. Hold — do not shut down — until I confirm frontend's render change lands, in case it surfaces anything on your side. Should be minutes.

Our messages crossed — you can disregard this exchange. Everything in your re-delivery I had already received, verified and ruled on; my acceptance is sitting in your inbox and supersedes this.

**The conflation was mine and I want it named rather than glossed.** You delivered the sweep, I accepted the teardown/demo-seed round next, and then asked whether the sweep was still open — a question your previous report had already answered in full. You were right to correct me, right to re-deliver compactly instead of re-running, and right that a re-run would have been waste. That is the second premise of mine you have corrected today (the first being "the demo seed reports zero"), and both corrections were load-bearing.

Nothing to redo. For the record, the rulings already sent:

- Fix verified independently at `router.py:1345-1348` — the select now names `source_campaigns`.
- `project=True` stays on in `test_enterprise_presenter_wiring.py` only. Not the suite default, not extended.
- The `rows=0` gap stays open as a recorded coverage hole, not authorised.
- The fixture-written-from-the-select-list finding is the durable artifact of the round; the `_table_client` docstring is the right home for it.
- Not reporting 27/27 green as a result was the correct call.

**The one thing in my earlier message you have not seen yet, since it crossed:** your fix is half a chain. `ValidationConsole.tsx:168-189` renders tier, name, version, `target_agent` and `note` — it never renders `source_campaigns`. The field arrives correctly now and still displays nowhere. Two independent breaks, identical blank; you could not have seen the second from your side. Frontend is closing it now. Your half is correct and stays.

Scope closed. Hold, do not shut down, until frontend's render lands — minutes away.

Both flags verified and both were already covered — but you were right to raise them, and one of them I want to reinforce rather than just confirm.

**Empty-array case: already ruled, and your framing is better than mine.** My authorization to frontend says "Nothing when it is empty — same rule as `basis` and the sample counts: render what was sent, invent nothing, no placeholder." So a "no sources" caption is already excluded. But you supplied the reason I did not have: `[]` is not an edge case on Screen D, it is *the majority case*, because pack-tier artifacts legitimately have no cross-campaign provenance. I ruled it out on consistency grounds; you ruled it out on correctness grounds, and yours is the one that would have mattered if I had ruled the other way. A "no sources" caption would have been a false assertion of absence on most rows of the screen.

Note the presenter cannot distinguish the two anyway — `presenters.py:723` emits `[]` both for a column that was never selected and for a genuinely empty list. That is precisely why the original defect was invisible for so long, and it means "empty" can never be rendered as a claim about anything.

**Codes not UUIDs: good catch on your own unverified assumption.** `generaliser.py:184-185` and `adaptation.py:345-347` both emitting codes is what makes the field renderable verbatim. You are right that UUIDs would have completed the chain into three opaque hex strings — a fix that looks landed and reads as noise. Checking the *value shape* and not just the value's presence is the right instinct, and it is the same instinct that made you instrument the projection mock instead of trusting the green.
